title: What is Deep Learning?
text:
What is Deep Learning?
Definition
Deep Learning is a subset of machine learning that uses artificial neural
networks with multiple layers (deep neural networks) to learn and make
decisions from data.
Key Characteristics
• Uses neural networks with many layers (hence ”deep”)
• Automatically learns hierarchical representations from data
• Can handle raw data directly (images, text, audio) without extensive
feature engineering
• Achieves state-of-the-art performance in many domains

text:
Basic Components of Deep Learning
Neural Network Architecture
• Input Layer: Receives raw data
• Hidden Layers: Learn hierarchical features
• Output Layer: Produces predictions
• Activation Functions: Introduce non-linearity (ReLU, Sigmoid, Tanh)
Training Process
• Loss Function: Measures prediction error
• Optimizer: Updates weights (SGD, Adam, etc.)
• Backpropagation: Computes gradients
• Epochs: Number of training iterations

title: Labels and Annotation

Labels and Annotation
Types of Labels
• Classification: Single or multiple class labels
• Regression: Continuous values (prices, scores)
• Detection: Bounding boxes with class labels
• Segmentation: Pixel-level masks
• Sequence labeling: Labels for each element in sequence

• Imbalanced classes: Unequal distribution
• Missing labels: Incomplete annotation
• Impact: Poor model performance, bias

title: Data Splits
text:
Data Splits
Train-Validation-Test Split
• Training set (70-80%): Model learning
• Validation set (10-15%): Hyperparameter tuning, model selection
• Test set (10-15%): Final evaluation (used only once)
Important Principles
• i.i.d. assumption: Independent and identically distributed
• No data leakage: Test set must be completely unseen
• Stratified sampling: Maintain class distribution in splits
• Time-aware splits: For time-series data, respect temporal order

title: Main Problem Types in Deep Learning
text:
Main Problem Types in Deep Learning
Supervised Learning Problems
• Classification: Assign discrete labels
• Binary: spam/not spam, cat/dog
• Multi-class: ImageNet (1000 classes), CIFAR-10 (10 classes)
• Multi-label: Multiple tags per sample
• Regression: Predict continuous values
• House price prediction, age estimation
• Time-series forecasting
• Object Detection: Locate and classify objects
• Bounding box coordinates + class labels
• YOLO, R-CNN, Faster R-CNN
• Segmentation: Pixel-level classification
• Semantic segmentation: Classify each pixel
• Instance segmentation: Separate object instances

dataset size).

title: k-Fold Cross Validation
text:
k-Fold Cross Validation
Idea
• Split dataset into k equally sized folds.
• Train on k −1 folds and validate on the remaining fold.
• Repeat k times, each fold serving as validation once.
• Average the evaluation metrics across all folds.
Final Step
• After model selection, retrain the chosen model on the entire dataset.
• Ensures best use of available data for deployment.
Benefit
• Every sample is used for both training and validation.
• Provides a more reliable estimate of model performance.

title: Bootstrap Evaluation
text:
Bootstrap Evaluation
Idea
• Resample the dataset with replacement to create many bootstrap
samples (each of size n).
• Train a model on each bootstrap sample and evaluate its performance.
• Aggregate the results to estimate performance and uncertainty.
Procedure
• Repeat for B bootstrap iterations (B=100∼1000):
• Draw a bootstrap sample of size n from the original data.
• Fit the model on the bootstrap sample.
• Evaluate using out-of-bag (OOB) data or an internal validation split.

title: Generalization and the Importance of Data
text:
Generalization and the Importance of Data
The Role of Data
• More high-quality and diverse data usually improves generalization.
• Data preprocessing (cleaning, normalization, augmentation) is as
important as model choice.
• Imbalanced or biased data leads to poor generalization, even with
powerful models.
• The diversity of training data determines how well the model performs in
the real world.
Key Message
Generalization depends not only on the algorithm but also heavily on the
quality, diversity, and representativeness of the data.

title: ROC-AUC: Computation and Notes
text:
ROC-AUC: Computation and Notes
• Sort samples by predicted score; sweep threshold to compute points
(FPR, TPR).
• Approximate area with the trapezoidal rule (sklearn does this by default).
• Robust to class-imbalance (uses ranking of scores rather than fixed
threshold).
• Multi-class: use one-vs-rest (macro/micro) averaging for ROC-AUC.
